name: Elecoglipron
lead: Elecoglipron (AZD5004, also ECC5004) is an investigational oral, small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist developed by AstraZeneca for weight management and type 2 diabetes. It is taken as a once-daily tablet without food or fluid restrictions. [1][2]

In a 36-week phase 2 trial in adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes (VISTA), mean weight change at week 26 ranged from -2.6% to -10.5% across dose groups versus -0.6% on placebo. In a phase 2b trial in type 2 diabetes (SOLSTICE), HbA1c fell by 0.91 to 1.88 percentage points versus 0.15 on placebo. Common adverse events were gastrointestinal. [1][2]
It is not approved. A large phase 3 programme in obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart failure and chronic kidney disease began in mid-2026. [3][4][5][6]

paras: Elecoglipron activates the GLP-1 receptor. A phase 1 open-label study in healthy participants compared the pharmacokinetics of two 50 mg formulations under fed and fasted conditions, reflecting the intent to dose without food restrictions. [7] A separate phase 1 study examines its effect on rosuvastatin and atorvastatin exposure. [8]

VISTA randomised 310 adults with obesity or overweight and at least one weight-related condition, without diabetes, to several dose levels and titration schedules or placebo for 36 weeks. At week 26, estimated mean weight change ranged from -2.6% (5 mg) to -10.5% (75 mg with weekly titration), compared with -0.6% on placebo. The share achieving at least 5% weight loss was 40.4% to 88.8% on drug versus 15.6% on placebo. [2]

Adverse events occurred in 84% to 98% of participants across drug groups and 84% on placebo; the most common were nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, headache and vomiting. The authors described the profile as consistent with the GLP-1 receptor agonist class. [2]

SOLSTICE enrolled 406 adults with type 2 diabetes, with an open-label oral semaglutide comparison arm. At week 26 HbA1c fell by 0.91% (5 mg) to 1.88% (75 mg with 2-week escalation) versus 0.15% on placebo. Adverse events ranged from 63% to 87% across elecoglipron groups versus 63% on placebo, mainly gastrointestinal. [1]

Registered phase 3 trials include a master protocol in obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes (4,500 participants) [5], an Asian-population obesity study [9], diabetes studies including a comparison with semaglutide and combinations with dapagliflozin [10][11][12][13], a heart failure outcomes trial (6,950) [3], and a chronic kidney disease outcomes trial (7,000) [4]. No phase 3 results had been published at the time of writing. A pooled analysis of oral non-peptide GLP-1 agonists in people without diabetes has been posted as a preprint. [14]

timeline.event: Phase 2 VISTA and SOLSTICE trials begin enrolling (October). [1][2]
Phase 2 results published in The Lancet; phase 3 trials start. [1][2][5]

card.summary: AstraZeneca's once-daily oral GLP-1 pill, with up to about 10% weight loss at 26 weeks in phase 2 and phase 3 now under way.

quick.overview:
Elecoglipron is an experimental oral GLP-1 agonist from AstraZeneca, taken once daily as a tablet with no food or fluid restrictions.

In a phase 2 obesity trial, average weight loss at 26 weeks reached 10.5% at the top dose versus 0.6% on placebo. A phase 2b diabetes trial showed HbA1c reductions up to 1.88 points.
quick.mechanism: It activates the GLP-1 receptor, the pathway used by semaglutide, but as a small-molecule non-peptide that can be swallowed.
quick.risks: Adverse events were mainly gastrointestinal: nausea, constipation, diarrhoea, headache and vomiting. Phase 3 trials are ongoing and it is not approved.
